title: Phasewise session stitch and SLO-driven egress for active-active gateway
creator: Lina Patel
description: Objective: implement an active-active failover pattern for the hosted API gateway that shifts traffic phasewise by session group while preserving streaming continuity and meeting latency/error SLOs. The feature must provide: (1) a telemetry-driven phase controller that decides cutover progress based on SLO and health signals, (2) a lightweight session "stitch" mechanism so in-flight streaming sessions can be continued on a target region without token loss, (3) circuit-breaker and load-shedding integration that applies both at egress and per-session levels, and (4) clear client-visible failure modes and retry semantics. The intent is to enable fast, predictable region handoffs during capacity events while minimizing client-visible errors and maintaining our 99.95% p50/p95 latency and 99.9% availability SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Phase controller can perform an incremental weight shift with 5% steps and pause/rollback based on SLO signals
During controlled failover tests, 99.95% of requests maintain p95 latency budget (per-route) and error rate stays within baseline plus 0.1% spike allowance
Ongoing streaming sessions started before shift are continued by a stitch path without token duplication or loss for at least 95% of sessions in synthetic tests
Circuit breakers trigger per-region and per-proxy with deterministic fallback to alternative region or preconfigured model variant within 200ms of threshold breach
When load-shedding is necessary, rejections return structured error with Retry-After and a per-session checkpoint URI so clients can resume or retry without full restart
Operational dashboards show cutover phases, per-session handoffs, and telemetry that drove pause/rollback decisions during the exercise
implementation_notes: Design summary: split cutover into two orthogonal planes: traffic shift (global weight delta using GSLB/Traffic Manager) and session continuity (proxy-level lightweight stitch). The phase controller consults a configurable SLO policy: latency SLOs, error budgets, CPU/GPU lane saturation, and KV-sync lag. On each phase step the controller computes a health vector and either proceed/pause/rollback. Session stitch: proxies export ephemeral session leases containing minimal KV summary (last prompt offset, KV-cache pointer, sequence nonce). Target-region proxies attempt a bounded pull-from-source via short-lived authenticated channel to reconstruct KV pointers and resume stream. If pull fails, session is either pinned back to origin or served degraded with best-effort partial history. Circuit breakers: layered - global (GSLB weight dampers), regional (egress queue depth), and per-proxy (latency/error windows). Load-shedding policy prefers graceful degrade (reject-with-checkpoint) before blunt connection drops. Observability: add "cutover-phase" span tag and per-session handoff events to tracing; emit metrics: handoff_success_rate, stitch_pull_latency, kv_sync_lag, phase_pause_reasons. Rollout plan: gated feature flag behind runtime-1.22; initial alpha in us-west/us-east with canary traffic 0.5% then expand to 10% following green signal.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC reviewed with Platform and SDK teams. Decided to use ephemeral session leases rather than full persisted snapshots to minimize storage churn. Action: eng to prototype lease format.
2026-03-11: Prototype of lease exchange implemented (PR 8201). Micro-benchmark shows stitch pull median 35ms across peered regions under low load.

2026-03-12: Load test v1 with synthetic streaming clients at 2x baseline showed stitch_success 92% with increased KV pull latency under burst. Decided to add backpressure threshold and fallback to origin pinning for sessions older than 90s.

2026-03-13: SLO policy draft accepted by SRE. Controller will use a 30s evaluation window on p95 latency and a 1m window on error rates. Next: integrate controller telemetry into Console cutover dashboard.
To do: add circuit-breaker mapping to model variants and implement structured rejection payload (spec attached).
